submissions.excerpt: If we get lucky, yet another 220k GB300 by late December
submissions.note: STATUS UPDATE on tracked project xAI Colossus 2 (slug xai-colossus-2-memphis; omitted projectId because this sandbox could not reach the live API today to look up the real DB id — see below). submissions.title: Pima County narrowly passes 120-day data center moratorium
submissions.excerpt: This moratorium shall apply to future development of new data centers where permits have not been issued for site improvements...
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION: Pima County, Arizona Board of Supervisors voted 3-2 (Tuesday, Sept 22, 2026) to adopt a 120-day moratorium on new data center development in unincorporated county areas, to allow time to draft new zoning rules and study public health impacts. The resolution as quoted in reporting also states data centers produce 'imminent negative public health impacts.' Projects that already have permits filed for site improvements (grading, paving, flood control, building construction) are exempt from the pause. I checked the nightly data/projects.json snapshot (103 projects) and did not find any tracked project sited in unincorporated Pima County, AZ, so this is not linked to an existing project. submissions.title: Georgia Residents Sue Over OpenAI Data Center
submissions.excerpt: A $20 billion data center campus announced in July near Rincon, Georgia, is now facing its second lawsuit from Effingham County residents and environmental advocates.
submissions.suggestedProjectName: OpenAI Project Gateway — Rincon, Georgia (Effingham County)
submissions.note: NEW PROJECT candidate, not found in the nightly data/projects.json snapshot (103 tracked projects, checked by name/location): a roughly $20B OpenAI data center campus (~4.4M sq ft reported) announced July 2026 near Rincon, Effingham County, Georgia — referred to in county records as 'Project Gateway' before OpenAI was publicly named as the tenant. SITING RESTRICTION-adjacent: the project is now facing its second lawsuit. This one (filed ~Sept 19-21, 2026, per The Current/Georgia Recorder/Inside Climate News) is from the Southern Environmental Law Center and the group One Hundred Miles, alleging the Effingham County Industrial Development Authority failed to properly notice the public ahead of its July approval vote (the item was reportedly listed on the meeting agenda only as 'Project Gateway,' without naming OpenAI or the tax break). A separate, earlier lawsuit from three Effingham County residents challenges the underlying zoning change. The $20B capex figure is press-reported and consistent across multiple outlets, but I could not trace it to a company or government filing today — LOW confidence.
